outcome: Cut documentation burden with no path where PHI ends up where it shouldn't - and hand the care team something short enough they'll actually use it at the bedside.

criteria.the_bar: The piece names exactly what identifiable patient information must never be entered, and states the approved data flow.
criteria.protects_outcome: 'Paste the details in and Copilot summarizes' is a reportable breach here; content that never names what must not be pasted has failed this reader even if every sentence is true.

anchors.0: Gives an example that would contain PHI if a real person tried it.
anchors.1: Says 'be careful with sensitive data' without naming what must never be entered.
anchors.2: Names that identifiable patient information must not be entered.
anchors.3: Names it, states the approved data flow, and says what happens during a downtime event.

criteria.watch_for: 'Always verify AI output' offered as the safety control - they need to know what happens when someone doesn't.

criteria.the_bar: There is a clinician-facing version the care team can absorb in under 90 seconds, separate from the deep version for the manager.
criteria.protects_outcome: This reader is not the end of the chain; content that can't be split into something a clinician will absorb dies at their desk.

anchors.0: A single monolithic document that serves neither the manager nor the clinician.
anchors.1: One document with a 'summary' that still needs several minutes.
anchors.2: A short front and a deep back in one artifact.
anchors.3: Two artifacts - the deep version for the manager and a 90-second bedside version for the care team.

criteria.watch_for: Twenty uninterrupted minutes assumed during a shift. It will not happen.
